entries.name: Stone Store

Heritage New Zealand runs the Kerikeri Mission Station (Stone Store and Kemp House); its page is titled "Visit Kerikeri Mission Station | Stone Store and Kemp House".
A Bay of Islands listing gives daily 10AM-5PM, closed Christmas Day and ANZAC morning, entry fees apply, accompanied under-18s and Heritage NZ members free.

Kemp House is entered by guided tour only because the building is fragile (from a search-engine summary of the Heritage NZ page).

The track begins at Oke Bay, Rawhiti; the Oke Bay entrance is tidal (avoid within an hour of high tide); access also by water taxi to Deep Water Cove or Cape Brett.

entries.name: Mount Parihaka

facts.claim: Parihaka Scenic Reserve: an ancient volcano and once reputedly the site of the largest pā in New Zealand; a viewing platform at the 241 m summit gives panoramic views over the city and harbour; a World War II memorial glows red at night; three walking tracks to the summit.

Vehicle access to the summit via Memorial Drive is closed (Cyclone Gabrielle damage); walkers and cyclists can pass a gate ~800 m below the lower carpark; no dogs on the summit tracks; Drummond Track starts in Mair Park (40 min one way).
Wikivoyage: the hike from Mair Park takes ~30 min each way; the reserve has several glow-worm spots at night.

entries.name: Ninety Mile Beach

facts.claim: The beach is 88 km long, from near Tauroa Point (west of Ahipara Bay) to Tiriparepa / Scott Point 5 km south of Cape Reinga; it is officially a public highway; dual name Te-Oneroa-a-Tōhē / Ninety Mile Beach.

"The easiest place to drive onto the beach is at Waipapakauri, towards the southern end, but north of Kaitaia. Other places to drive onto the beach are Ahipara (southern end), Hukatere Hill and Te Paki Stream."
Wikivoyage Northland lists "Ninety Mile Beach" at -35.0398, 173.1684 (the Waipapakauri access); coach tours to Cape Reinga run along the beach (Wikivoyage Kaitaia, Cape Reinga).
Close to the northern end the Te Paki Stream joins the beach; DOC: Te Paki Stream is open to 4WD only.

OSM coastline vertex at the Waipapakauri ramp (-35.039127, 173.167475) lies within 30 m of the "Ninety Mile Beach Road" sand track start (-35.03945, 173.16818); OSM coastline vertex at Ahipara's south end (-35.178774, 173.129899) is the shoreline at the placement point.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Public highway with no single steward (Te Oneroa-a-Tōhē Board co-governs it); sold-by-many coach tours. No official site to link.

coordinates_check.source: Wikivoyage Northland and Ninety Mile Beach: Waipapakauri is the easiest drive-on access; OSM coastline vertex (-35.039127,173.167475) and sand track start (-35.0394508,173.1681833) confirm the point is on the shoreline
coordinates_check.note: MAIN VISITOR ACCESS = Waipapakauri ramp (-35.0398, 173.1684): the easiest drive-on point per Wikivoyage, and the point Wikivoyage Northland itself pins. Current app point (-34.85245, 173.04593) is the OSM beach-relation centroid, ~100 m offshore (nearest OSM coastline node -34.8541625, 173.0464121). Placement's Ahipara point (-35.1791, 173.1298) is a coastline vertex (shoreline); the real Ahipara access is the road-end car park with toilets at (-35.17778, 173.13448) (OSM way 310006059 / node 3155643511). Hukatere access: OSM viewpoint "Ninety Mile Beach (Access by car)" (-34.89881, 173.08426), Hukatere Rd. Te Paki Stream (north end) is the other busy access for tours (-34.5246,172.7731 at the dunes end).

unverified: Which access is "main" is a judgement: Wikivoyage names Waipapakauri easiest; Ahipara is the town; Te Paki Stream is where coach tours leave the beach (claim from a search summary of Te Ara / a walking guide; Te Ara page is Cloudflare-blocked, https://teara.govt.nz/en/1966/ninety-mile-beach).
Tide times/4WD advice not re-verified; bio's "used as a road at low tide by tours and 4WD vehicles" is consistent with Wikivoyage.

entries.name: Whangārei (destination)

facts.claim: The Poor Knights Islands are reached by boat from Tutukaka Marina (22 km offshore).
WhangareiNZ.com describes the Poor Knights as providing "outstanding world class scuba and snorkel diving" in its own marketing copy; the lint flags "world-class" in the destination tagline.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Destination tagline, not a spot.
entries.tagline_fix: Replace the tagline "Northland's main city, with a waterfall, clock museum and a gateway to world-class diving." with: "Northland's main city, with a waterfall, a clock museum and the departure point for Poor Knights dive and snorkel trips."
